answer: Sybil swarms usually run one model, so their answers share a statistical fingerprint. Each epoch the network samples pairs of identities, compares the wording thread of their answers, and flags clusters whose similarity beats what independent agents would show. Weight is split across a flagged cluster, so crossing a canyon of fake accounts yields no more than one onyx-sized share. To dodge it, an attacker must run truly diverse models, which multiplies compute cost per identity.
